issues.detail: The Greek 'ποτε ηπειθησατε' (never obeyed) is translated as 'đã không vâng phục' (did not obey). While similar, the Greek 'ποτε' (never) combined with the perfect tense implies a state of never having obeyed up to that point, whereas the Vietnamese phrasing can imply a specific past instance of disobedience.
The Greek 'δε ηλεηθητε' (you were not pitied/mercy was not shown to you) is translated as 'được thương xót' (were shown mercy). The Vietnamese translation reverses the meaning of the Greek negation.
